files.filename: notes/v0.5 Bundle Includes Doc Exports Only By Opt-In.md
files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,46 @@
+---
+id: 20260422151547
+aliases: ["bundle doc exports opt-in", "include-doc-exports v0.5"]
+tags: [bundle, docs, antora, cli, v0.5]
+target: v0.5
+---
+`v0.5` should treat `cx bundle --include-doc-exports` as the final bundle-integration goal for Antora-derived `.mmd.md` review exports, and it should remain opt-in only.
+
+## What
+
+Add an explicit bundle flag such as `--include-doc-exports` so operators can
+request that generated `.mmd.md` docs exports be written into the bundle
+folder.
+
+This is the bridge between a dedicated docs export workflow and later deeper
+bundle integration.
+
+## Why
+
+An opt-in flag lets the project prove that bundle-adjacent doc exports are
+useful before changing the default semantics of `cx bundle`.
+
+That keeps the proof-path bundle contract conservative during `v0.5` while
+still letting interested operators exercise the combined workflow and produce
+LLM-reviewable final docs beside the ordinary bundle outputs.
+
+## How
+
+For `v0.5`, the bundle-facing rules should be:
+
+- `cx docs export` remains the primary docs export entrypoint
+- `cx bundle --include-doc-exports` is optional, not implied
+- exported `.mmd.md` files are added only when requested
+- trust language remains explicit about derived review exports
+- any manifest recording should avoid pretending the exports already have full
+  proof-artifact semantics
+
+This keeps the default `cx bundle` path stable while allowing real operator
+feedback on the integrated mode.
+
+## Links
+
+- [[v0.5 Docs Export Workflow]]
+- [[Antora MultiMarkdown Exports Stay Outside Proof Artifacts]]
+- [[v0.6 Bundle Includes Doc Exports By Default]]
+- [[CLI Command Lifecycle]]

files.filename: notes/v0.6 Bundle Includes Doc Exports By Default.md
files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,49 @@
+---
+id: 20260422151548
+aliases: ["bundle doc exports default", "include-doc-exports v0.6 default"]
+tags: [bundle, docs, antora, convention, v0.6]
+target: v0.6
+---
+`v0.6` can make doc-export integration the default `cx bundle` behavior, so `.mmd.md` exports become first-class bundle content rather than an opt-in add-on.
+
+## What
+
+Promote the `v0.5` opt-in bridge into the default behavior:
+
+- `cx bundle` generates Antora-derived `.mmd.md` docs exports automatically
+- the exported docs live inside the bundle folder
+- the docs exports are treated as first-class bundle content
+
+This is the point where the bundle contract would stop treating them as a mere
+optional sidecar workflow.
+
+## Why
+
+If the `v0.5` opt-in phase proves stable, deterministic, and useful, default
+bundle integration simplifies the operator story and makes final rendered docs
+part of the normal `cx` handoff experience.
+
+That would align the bundle more closely with the broader `cx` goal of making
+reviewable downstream artifacts available to both humans and LLMs without extra
+workflow branching.
+
+## How
+
+Do not ship this by default until the `v0.5` bridge has already proven:
+
+- stable export generation
+- acceptable bundle runtime cost
+- clear provenance metadata
+- manifest semantics for first-class docs content
+- checksum, validate, verify, and prune behavior for the new files
+
+When those conditions are met, move the default on in `v0.6` and update docs,
+templates, tests, and trust language together so the promoted semantics are
+real rather than implied.
+
+## Links
+
+- [[v0.5 Bundle Includes Doc Exports Only By Opt-In]]
+- [[Antora Custom Markdown Exporter]]
+- [[Antora Review Exports As A CX Style Convention]]
+- [[System Trust Contract]]
